headline: Micronesia's Internet Revolution: From $705/Mbps to Pennies
meta_description: After ending its government telecom monopoly in 2014, the Federated States of Micronesia saw internet access skyrocket 20-fold and costs plummet 99%.
summary_short: When Micronesia ended its telecom monopoly, internet access jumped 20-fold and costs fell 99%—connecting remote island communities to essential services.
body:
For decades, the Federated States of Micronesia—an archipelago of over 600 islands scattered across 2.9 million square kilometers of ocean—relied on a single government-controlled provider for all telecommunications. When that monopoly ended in 2014 following World Bank urging, the results were transformative: internet access increased 2,000%, reaching 88% of the population, while monthly broadband costs collapsed from $65 per megabit to just 78 cents. Mobile internet data, which once cost $705 per megabyte-per-second, now costs $30. Competition brought new providers including Kacific, Starlink Pacific, and iSolutions Micronesia into the market, spurring innovation that had been suppressed for three decades.

The real breakthrough came through satellite technology, which had languished under the old system. Advanced satellite networks now serve the most remote islands, while over 1,500 kilometers of undersea fiber optic cables have been laid across the archipelago. This infrastructure has enabled vital digital services in healthcare, voting, and digital identification—amenities that were simply inaccessible when connectivity was expensive and scarce.

Beyond FSM's borders, the transformation has rippled outward. The archipelago became a landing point for the East Micronesia Cable system, extending improved connectivity to neighboring Kiribati and Nauru. The World Bank's Digital FSM Project, launched in 2020, continues supporting this technological integration. What began as a simple policy change—ending one company's stranglehold on telecommunications—has become a template for how breaking monopolies can unlock opportunity across isolated communities.
quick_facts: Internet costs fell 99%: from $65/Mbps to 78 cents monthly
Over 600 islands in Federated States of Micronesia now connected
Access increased 2,000% to reach 88% of population by 2014
1,500+ kilometers of undersea fiber cables laid since monopoly ended
Mobile data costs dropped from $705/Mbps to $30
